core.title: Use singular aspects for item schemas and correctly pluralized aspects for collections
core.given: An artifact name's aspect refers to a schema that is either a single item or a collection (e.g. in a plan artifact, an acceptance artifact, a doc, or the schema itself)
core.when: the planner writes, renames or checks that aspect, or the schema's item/collection shape changes
core.then: Use the singular aspect for an item schema and the plural aspect for a collection schema, following English pluralization rules.
prefer: Irregular: English irregular form (analysis->analyses, policy->policies, datum->data, index->indices, child->children).
Uncountable: explicit suffix (config vs config.collection; data.item vs data.items).
Compound: pluralize the primary noun (button-group->button-groups, session-state->session-states).
avoid: Plural aspect on an item schema, or singular aspect on a collection schema.
Naive 's' plurals of irregular nouns (analysiss, policys, childs).
An uncountable collection aspect without an explicit suffix (e.g. bare config or data for a collection); a bare item like config is fine.
Pluralizing a non-primary noun of a compound name.
core.why: Cardinality is read from the aspect's singular/plural form, so correct plurals keep the item-vs-collection signal reliable.
evidence: Every artifact aspect in scope is singular when its schema is a single item and plural when its schema is a collection.
Each plural aspect follows the applicable rule: regular +s, English irregular form, explicit suffix for uncountables, or pluralized primary noun for compounds.
verification: A check applies the four pluralization categories to every aspect: regular (+s), English irregular form, explicit collection suffix for uncountable nouns, and pluralizing the primary noun of a compound.

A check compares each aspect's grammatical number with its schema's shape (item vs collection), covering existing as well as new or renamed names and schema-only shape changes, and flags irregular nouns pluralized with plain 's'.

For uncountable nouns, a collection aspect must carry an explicit collection suffix; any uncountable collection aspect without one is flagged even if it is otherwise distinguishable from the item. Accepted patterns: a bare item with a suffixed collection, or a suffixed item with a suffixed collection.
Deciding whether a schema is an item or a collection, and whether a plural is correct English, is not mechanically decidable in general; it needs judgement or a dictionary-backed check.

values: schema shape changed between item and collection
existing artifact name present in touched artifact
aspect number does not match schema cardinality
uncountable collection aspect lacks explicit suffix

fires: An artifact's schema describes a single item and its aspect is (or would be) written in the plural.
An artifact's schema describes a collection and its aspect is singular or wrongly pluralized.
An existing artifact name is checked or touched and its aspect number does not match its schema cardinality.
A schema changes between item and collection without its aspect changing (schema-only cardinality change).
A collection aspect is formed from an irregular, uncountable or compound noun.
doesNotFire: Naming of things that are not artifacts with an aspect segment (e.g. prose headings, code variable names).
Edits that touch no artifact name and no schema item/collection shape.

neutralityNotes: This convention is a linguistic naming rule (English pluralization of an artifact name's aspect segment) and is stack-neutral by nature; the core carries the full obligation without any profile data, so profileRequirements and proposedKeys are empty. The only Bun-local content is the illustrative document-kind lists in 'given' and activation.facts[1] ('wagon', 'WMBT'), which are explicitly non-exclusive examples and are preserved in bunOnly. The prefer/avoid word examples (fragment->fragments, config.collection, button-group) are retained because they express the normative pluralization categories of the naming convention, not stack constructs. Sidecar 'note' fields on activation facts are explanatory commentary and are not part of the core fact schema; their normative content survives via the observability values and core:verification.
